title: Finite coefficient and site extension on bounded flat input models
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), let $\ell$ be a prime, and let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$. Use ordinary constant-ring module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $a\le b$ be integers and let $L\in D^b(X_{\rm et},A)$ have constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, meaning that $L\otimes^L_A H[0]$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ for every etale module sheaf $H$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Write $N_X=\nu_X^*$ for exact site comparison and $L_B=L\otimes^L_A B$ [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor].
There is a flat constructible complex $P$, zero outside $[a,b]$, representing $L$. It is K-flat (tensoring it with any acyclic complex is acyclic). The complexes $P\otimes_A B$, $N_XP$, and $(N_XP)\otimes_A B$ are K-flat with flat terms and vanish outside $[a,b]$; they represent respectively $L_B$, $N_XL$, and $(N_XL)_B$. The canonical tensor comparison identifies the last complex with $N_X(P\otimes_A B)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Both $L_B$ and $N_XL$ are bounded constructible of Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ on their respective sites, as is $(N_XL)_B$ [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is required. Flatness and K-flatness use [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Schemes and Noetherian rings use [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings), bounded finite-Tor domain verification; the flat-model and constructibility assertions are an agent deduction from the separately cited nodes, not statements of this remark.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] with $\Lambda=A$, $K=L$ and the given integers $a\leq b$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $A$ is finite, $X$ is Noetherian, and $L$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. It supplies a complex $P$ whose terms are flat constructible $A_X$-module sheaves, with $P^q=0$ outside $[a,b]$, and an isomorphism $L\simeq P$ in the derived category. This chooses the one input model used throughout the proof.

source.place: hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flatConstructibleModel, lines 160-209; the existing DAG theorem is used as a black box

proof.text: The bound $P^q=0$ for $q>b$ makes $P$ a bounded-above complex of flat module sheaves. Thus [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes it K-flat on the ringed small etale site $(X_{\rm et},A_X)$. This is K-flatness against arbitrary acyclic complexes, not just bounded acyclic test complexes.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, label lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat (the cited node has the older incorrect tag 06YS in its source field, but its statement is precisely this lemma)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] to the identity topos with ring map $A_X\to B_X$, and to the site comparison with its constant-ring identification from [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Starting with $P$, these applications give K-flatness and flat terms for $P\otimes_A B$ and $N_XP$; applying the identity-topos change of rings on the pro-etale site to $N_XP$ gives them for $(N_XP)\otimes_A B$. All these functors send zero modules to zero modules, so the degree interval stays $[a,b]$. The computing comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], applied to the two coefficient morphisms, identifies the first and third complexes with $L_B$ and $(N_XL)_B$. Exactness in [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] identifies termwise $N_XP$ with $N_XL$: it sends the isomorphism represented by $P$ to its derived isomorphism. No coefficient ring map in the K-flat pullback statement is assumed flat.

source.place: Tags 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat) and 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), applied to the identity-topos coefficient morphisms and the comparison morphism

proof.text: For every degree $q$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] to $P^q$ and the etale $A_X$-module $B_X$. The constant-module isomorphism of [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module], with $R=A$ and $M=B$, identifies $N_XB_X$ with the pro-etale $B_X$, including its $A$-action. Hence the canonical comparison gives $N_X(P^q\otimes_A B)\simeq N_XP^q\otimes_A B$. It is $B_X$-linear: scalar multiplication by a section of $B_X$ acts on the second tensor factor on both sides. Naturality in $P^q$ makes the isomorphisms commute with the differentials, giving the asserted isomorphism of complexes. Its image in the derived category is the canonical derived tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]: that node defines the comparison on K-flat representatives by these same termwise tensor maps. In particular the fourth complex also represents $(N_XL)_B$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, label lemma-tensor-product-pullback; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product, its comparison on K-flat representatives

proof.text: Fix a degree $q$ and a finite constructible stratification witnessing constructibility of $P^q$ in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. On a stratum $i:S\to X$ the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] identifies $i^*(P^q\otimes_A B)$ with $i^*P^q\otimes_A i^*B_X$, and the constant-module isomorphism of [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] (with $R=A$, $M=B$, $f=i$) identifies $i^*B_X$ with $B_S$, compatibly with the $B$-action by its naturality in the $A$-linear maps $b\cdot-:B\to B$; so $i^*(P^q\otimes_A B)\simeq i^*P^q\otimes_A B_S$. The scalar-extension clause of [lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension] makes this a finite locally constant $B_S$-module: on a trivializing etale cover it has value $M\otimes_A B$ for a finite $A$-module $M$. Concretely, if $r$ elements generate $M$, their tensors with $1$ generate $M\otimes_A B$ over the finite ring $B$, so its underlying set is finite. Empty strata give the zero sheaf and need no choice of a geometric point; on every nonempty stratum a geometric point exists, as in the lisse lemma. Thus the same finite partition witnesses constructibility over $B$ for each term of $P\otimes_A B$.

source.place: Tag 0GKB, label lemma-tensor-constructible, same-stratification argument; the local scalar-extension input is the existing lisse lemma

proof.text: Put $Q=P\otimes_A B$. By Step 5 its terms are constructible $B_X$-modules. Apply [thm-constructible-serre] over the finite ring $B$: $Z^q=\ker(Q^q\to Q^{q+1})$ is constructible, and $H^q(Q)=\operatorname{coker}(Q^{q-1}\to Z^q)$ is constructible. These are maps between constructible sheaves, so the kernel and cokernel clauses apply directly. Since $Q$ is zero outside $[a,b]$, so is its cohomology. Step 3 therefore proves bounded constructibility of $L_B$.

source.place: Tag 03RZ, label lemma-constructible-abelian, kernel and cokernel clauses

proof.text: The given finite affine cover makes $X$ quasi-compact. It is locally Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes it quasi-separated. Each finite coefficient ring is Noetherian, since it has only finitely many ideals. Consequently the forward constructible-sheaf comparison in [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] applies to both $A$ and $B$. Exactness of $N_X$ in [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] gives $H^q(N_XL)\simeq N_XH^q(L)$, so $N_XL$ is bounded constructible. Apply the same statements over $B$ to the bounded constructible etale complex $L_B$ obtained in Step 6. This gives bounded constructibility of $N_XL_B$, hence of $(N_XL)_B$ by Step 4. To check the global finite-stratification convention explicitly, take the finite stratification of each etale cohomology sheaf. For each stratum $i:S\to X$, [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies $i^*N_XF$ with $N_Si^*F$. A trivializing etale covering is also a pro-etale covering, and [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] identifies its constant values with the same finite modules. Thus that same finite partition witnesses the pro-etale constructibility required here.

source.place: forward directions of (1) and (2); locally Noetherian quasi-separatedness is the separately cited scheme lemma

proof.text: Finally apply the implication from a flat model to Tor amplitude in [lem-sp-ringed-site-tor-flat-model], on $(X_{\rm et},B_X)$, $(X_{\rm proet},A_X)$, and $(X_{\rm proet},B_X)$ respectively. Step 3 has supplied, for $L_B$, $N_XL$ and $(N_XL)_B$, flat representatives zero outside $[a,b]$. The cited equivalence therefore gives Tor amplitude in precisely this interval for all three objects, against every module sheaf on the appropriate site. Together with Steps 1-7 this proves every claim. In particular $B$ itself is never used as a K-flat or flat $A$-module: only $P$ and its pullbacks are used to compute the derived extensions.
